slides.title: Timo, the In-Car AI Social Robot, Launches on Kickstarter
slides.highlight: Timo is an in-car AI social robot, providing a relevant example of embodied social robotics for RwB.

slides.title: Former Li Auto AI Chief Scientist Chen Wei Raises Funds for Embodied AI Home Robot Startup
slides.tldr: FUNDING FOR EMBODIED AI HOME ROBOTS
slides.highlight: Chen Wei has raised funds for an embodied AI startup focused on home robots, aligning with RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: ABM-SIRTEM: A Hybrid Agent-Based and Epidemiological Model for Pandemic Response
slides.highlight: This research introduces ABM-SIRTEM, a hybrid model integrating individual-level economic productivity and welfare with disease dynamics. It is relevant to MIMIC for its approach to simulating the interaction between socioeconomic behavior and societal-scale impacts.

card.one_liner: ABM-SIRTEM is a hybrid model coupling population-level disease dynamics with agent-based socioeconomic behavior and compliance.
card.key_idea: It integrates the SIRTEM epidemiological model with an agent-based model where compliance evolves via evolutionary game theory based on economic productivity, mental well-being, and health risks.
card.evaluation: Calibrated using Bayesian optimization against historical COVID-19 positive/negative test counts from four U.S. states; results broadly reproduce timing of observed waves.
card.limitation: Evaluations assess calibration fit rather than performance on held-out data; the model does not establish causality between infections and policy changes.

slides.title: ECHO: A Matched-Contrast Benchmark for Context-Sensitive Turn-Taking in Full-Duplex Dialogue
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark for distinguishing between interruptions and backchannels in full-duplex dialogue, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: ECHO is a diagnostic benchmark for Chinese full-duplex dialogue to evaluate context-sensitive turn-taking decisions.
card.key_idea: It uses matched-contrast pairs where the same user utterance is paired with different dialogue contexts to distinguish between interruptions (Yield) and backchannels/off-talk (Keep).
card.evaluation: Evaluated four speech systems and Gemini (text reference) using Pairwise Action Success Rate (PASR). Most speech systems showed a strong Yield bias.
card.limitation: Uses synthesized audio rather than natural speech, and interruption waveforms include label-dependent acoustic cues like onset emphasis.

slides.title: A Deployable Architecture for Robot-Mediated Tasks (DART): Evaluation in Socially Assistive Robot-Guided Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Exercises
slides.highlight: DART provides a cloud-based architecture to extend low-cost socially assistive robots with web applications for health interventions, supporting the RwB goal of embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: DART extends low-cost socially assistive robots using a web application and cloud infrastructure for complex tasks.
card.key_idea: A robot-agnostic architecture distributing interaction orchestration to a web app, data/computation to the cloud, and physical embodiment to the robot via MQTT.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via participatory design, a 103-participant in-lab study (showing reduced stress/anxiety), and a six-week in-home deployment with four participants.
card.limitation: Participants identified speech input, visual presentation, and web-robot synchronization as priority areas for improvement.

slides.title: Audio-Visual Turn-taking Prediction in Cocktail Party Scenarios
slides.highlight: This research evaluates audio-visual predictive turn-taking models in noisy cocktail-party scenarios, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling in complex environments.

card.one_liner: Audio-visual turn-taking models degrade in cocktail-party scenarios, but fine-tuning on noisy data improves robustness.
card.key_idea: Evaluates Voice Activity Projection (VAP) variants (Audio, Video, Multimodal) by pre-training on clean Candor data and fine-tuning on the noisy AVCocktail dataset.
card.evaluation: Tested on Candor and AVCocktail using weighted F1 scores. Results show a relative weighted F1 drop up to 38% under noise.
card.limitation: Fine-tuning causes catastrophic forgetting of clean domains; high-level OpenFace features and current fusion mechanisms limit peak performance.

slides.title: Exploring Multimodal Turn-Taking Cues in Face-to-Face Conversation using Voice Activity Projection
slides.highlight: This research investigates how visual features like gaze, head movement, and facial action units enhance turn-taking prediction, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: Visual cues from face-to-face conversations significantly improve turn-taking prediction over audio-only models.
card.key_idea: Extends the Voice Activity Projection (VAP) transformer by fusing audio with visual features (FAU, gaze, head, body) using cross-attention, delta motion features, and trainable gating.
card.evaluation: Tested on 400h of Meta Seamless Interaction dataset using VAP loss and balanced accuracy for hold/shift, short/long, and pre-shift tasks; results are statistically significant.
card.limitation: Evaluation is not dyad-disjoint, potentially exploiting dyad-specific regularities; gaze estimates are unreliable during eye occlusion.

slides.title: MP-Bench: Evaluating Voice Agents as a Multiparty Conversation Participant
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR MULTIPARTY VOICE AGENT EVALUATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces MP-Bench to evaluate voice agents' turn-taking awareness and response appropriateness in multi-party contexts, supporting HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: MP-Bench evaluates voice agents' ability to actively participate in multiparty conversations via turn-taking and comprehension.
card.key_idea: A benchmark using synthetic audio scenarios (Discussion and Turn-based Game) to test turn-taking awareness (explicit, implicit, negative) and contextual response appropriateness across 12 voice agents.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 12 agents using LLM-as-a-judge and human verification. Realtime agents performed near-chance on implicit turn-taking and below 33% on multiparty comprehension.
card.limitation: Uses synthetic audio without overlapping speech, background noise, or multi-turn engagement, potentially underestimating real-world complexity.

slides.title: PRISM: Predictive Representation of Interaction Style and Motion for Social Robot Navigation
slides.highlight: PRISM uses a transformer encoder to infer human interaction traits from passive observations, improving collision rates and navigation efficiency in crowds. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and social robots.

card.one_liner: PRISM infers human interaction styles from passive observations to improve social robot navigation in crowds.
card.key_idea: A transformer encoder uses Rank-N-Contrast loss to map trajectories into a continuous ordinal latent space, providing style vectors and temporal confidence scores to a navigation policy.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in PyBullet simulations with ORCA pedestrians; PRISM reduced collision rates (e.g., 0.19 to 0.12 in training distribution) compared to the HEIGHT baseline.
card.limitation: Results are based on synthetic ORCA parameters; lacks real-world pedestrian data, confidence intervals, and closed-loop component ablations.
